note: Acrostic praise: the human praise-operations across the alphabet, movement-anchored

dims.v: the self resolves to extol and bless God's name for ever and ever - praise as vow
v1: 'I will EXTOL you, my God and King, and BLESS your name forever' - the interior binds itself to unending praise, the acrostic's opening pledge.
every single day the self will bless and praise - praise made a daily discipline
v2: 'EVERY DAY I will BLESS you' - distinct from the forever-vow: praise distributed into the grain of ordinary time, a habit not just an oath.
one generation commends God's works to the next - praise handed forward as inheritance
v4: 'One generation shall COMMEND your works to another' - the operation reaches beyond the self: praise as a relay across time.
the self meditates on the glorious splendour and wondrous works of God
v5: 'I will MEDITATE on your wondrous works' - the interior dwells, ponders, feeds attention on God's majesty.
the self declares God's mighty, awesome deeds - proclamation of his greatness
v6: 'they shall speak of the might of your AWESOME DEEDS, and I will DECLARE your greatness' - the interior overflows into public telling.
the self pours forth the fame of God's abundant goodness and sings of his righteousness
v7: 'they shall POUR FORTH the fame of your abundant goodness and SING of your righteousness' - the operation is exuberant overflow, memory of goodness spilling into song.
all God's works give thanks and his saints bless him - the community's gratitude
v10: 'all your works shall GIVE THANKS to you, and your SAINTS shall BLESS you' - the interior of the whole godly community turns grateful.
the saints speak of the glory of God's kingdom and tell of his power
v11: 'they shall speak of the GLORY of your kingdom and TELL of your power' - the interior makes known God's reign to the children of man.
the operation of calling on God sincerely, in truth - not mere formula but real appeal
v18: 'the LORD is near to all who CALL on him, to all who call on him in TRUTH' - the interior condition that draws God near is truthful calling.
the reverent fear of God whose desire he fulfils and whose cry he hears and saves
v19: 'he fulfils the DESIRE of those who FEAR him; he also hears their cry and saves them' - the interior posture of fear is met with fulfilment and rescue.
the love of God that he preserves - the interior attachment God guards
v20: 'the LORD preserves all who LOVE him' - the operation is the self's fastening onto God in love, answered by preservation.
the closing resolve: the self's mouth speaks praise, and all flesh will bless God's holy name forever
v21: 'My MOUTH will speak the PRAISE of the LORD, and let all FLESH BLESS his holy name forever' - the acrostic closes by widening the self's praise to all creation.
v8: 'The LORD is GRACIOUS and merciful' - the goodness the psalmist pours forth.
v8: 'MERCIFUL, slow to anger' - God's compassion praised.
v8: 'abounding in STEADFAST LOVE' - the covenant loyalty sung.
v9: 'The LORD is GOOD to all' - the goodness the saints thank him for.
v9: 'his MERCY is over all that he has made' - the compassion evoking thanks.
v13: 'The LORD is FAITHFUL in all his words' - the reliability told of the kingdom.
v13: 'KIND in all his works' - God's graciousness in the kingdom-telling.
v14: 'The LORD UPHOLDS all who are falling' - the support the God-fearer relies on.
v14: 'RAISES up all who are bowed down' - God's lifting act.
v16: 'you SATISFY the DESIRE of every living thing' - the provision the fear waits on.
v18: 'The LORD is NEAR to all who call on him' - the nearness truthful calling meets.
v20: 'the LORD PRESERVES all who love him' - the keeping love is answered with.
v19: 'he HEARS their cry and saves them' - God's response to the fearers.
v19: 'he FULFILS the desire of those who fear him' - the answered longing.
v4: 'they shall DECLARE your mighty acts' - part of the generational commending.
v12: 'to make KNOWN to the children of man his mighty deeds' - the aim of the telling.
